title: RWB-S5-E4031-APP: the RAMC transfer step has no source for its call names, its pool, price and approval references, its timer or its screen owner
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5, R7.3 and R9; split_plan.json slices RWB-S5-E4031-APP and -CON (H, C, I, X); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 19, 41, 43 and 44; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 13, 14 and 28; Ownership Map v1 rows asset_sale, listing, asset, recovery_case, assignment, approval, rule_row, partner_instruction and template; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DIS-23, R-DIS-59 and R-DIS-60; TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 T2, T3.1, T3.2, T3.3, T4, T6.1 and T-A.1; FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 A2.22; legacy RWB-E4-031
description: (1) No source publishes the element names or the acceptance and refusal codes of the rwb-partner issueInstruction activity, and no source publishes the name of the rwb-case case-move answer; Architecture v5 slide 19 OUT gives the activity name only. (2) The transfer record has no table of its own and no column for the pool, the transfer-price template version or the committee-approval reference: asset_sale is the sale table of TSD S5 T3.1 (DF-SAL-009 to DF-SAL-019) and the Ownership Map table list has neither a RAMC transfer table nor a pool table, although LOV-SALE-CHANNEL carries the RAMC value. (3) Architecture v5 slide 19 OUT gives Decision: child: approval and the Ownership Map gives approval to P7, but no source says whether the committee approval is the P7 ApprovalWorkflow, what it decides or whether a REST approval operation exists. (4) The R-DIS-59 timer cell reads per agreement and no source gives it a duration or a unit, while the rule row and its timer specification are governed in rwb-decision. (5) PRT-06 Transfer confirmation has states but no named owner, and SCR-21 is a Workbench screen behind gateway-bff while the partner portal is served with rwb-partner. (6) The plan gives H of three rows and C, I and X empty, although the step also consumes rwb-partner, rwb-case, rwb-decision and rwb-source-data rows.
evidence: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 row R-DIS-59 with Timer cell per agreement and Systems cell Partner Portal, Calculation Service; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DIS-23 (route = RAMC and committee approved, to ROUTE_APPROVED_RAMC) and R-DIS-60 (TRANSFER_COMPLETED to ASSET_TRANSFERRED); Architecture v5 slide 19 OUT line TMP Partner: issueInstruction (auction vendor) · Decision: child: approval; Architecture v5 slide 43 rows 22 and AssetSold; Ownership Map v1 api rows POST /cases/{caseId}/instructions and GET /partner/instructions with owner S9; Ownership Map v1 tables approval, rule_row and decision_log_entry owner P7, partner_instruction owner S9, template owner P6; TSD S5 v2 T3.1 asset_sale DF-SAL-009 to DF-SAL-019 with no pool, price-version or approval column and T3.2 LOV-SALE-CHANNEL with the value RAMC; FSD S5 v3 A2.22.3.2 field catalog and A2.22.4.4 no background event; split_plan.json slice RWB-S5-E4031-APP with H of three rows and C, I, X empty
area: Contract, data model, approval boundary, timer and screens
proposed: Read the defaults recorded in ASM-B-S5-05-E4031-1, keep them in the RWB-S5-E4031-CON baseline, and confirm the partner, case and approval names with S9, P3 and P7 before the baseline is tagged; raise the missing transfer table and the three missing columns to the Ownership Map owner if the reading is not accepted

title: RWB-S5-E4031-APP: the legacy endpoints name an S1 operation and a later S5 pricing operation, neither of which the transfer step calls
source: legacy RWB-E4-031 Endpoints and Permission checks tables; TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 T-A.1 and T6.1; Ownership Map v1 api rows POST /assets/{assetId}/valuations and POST /assets/{assetId}/listings with their rulings ASM-A6-api-6 and ASM-A6-api-15; FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 A2.22.3.3
description: The legacy Endpoints table lists POST /assets/{assetId}/valuations (API-S5-003, now rwb-valuation's under the Ownership Map ruling ASM-A6-api-6) and POST /assets/{assetId}/listings (API-S5-004, the pricing story's) with the right Asset and disposal C, and the legacy Permission checks table grants C for them. The transfer of a pool to RAMC calls neither operation, and the two operations this step does provide are the reads behind PRT-06 and SCR-21, which TSD S5 T-A.1 gives right R. The legacy rows therefore describe a surface this story does not own, and no source says which operation the C right of the feature attaches to.
evidence: legacy RWB-E4-031 Endpoints table rows POST /api/recovery/v1/assets/{assetId}/valuations and POST /api/recovery/v1/assets/{assetId}/listings with access Asset and disposal C; legacy RWB-E4-031 Permission checks table with right C; TSD S5 v2 T-A.1 rows API-S5-001 and API-S5-002 with right R and API-S5-003 to API-S5-005 with rights C and U; Ownership Map v1 api rows POST /assets/{assetId}/valuations owner S1 (ruling ASM-A6-api-6) and POST /assets/{assetId}/listings owner S5 (ruling ASM-A6-api-15); FSD S5 v3 A2.22.3.3 roles Sale officer primary and Head of NPA, RAMC user also uses
proposed: Name the two legacy endpoints in the story as operations of their owners that are not built here, declare only the two reads as provided with right R, and grant no C right to this step

title: RWB-S5-E4031-APP: the split plan and TSD S5 T8 carry no requirement id for FEAT-AST-22
source: split_plan.json slice RWB-S5-E4031-APP reqs; legacy_index.json RWB-E4-031 reqs; TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 T8 requirement traceability; FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 A2.22.1 and the Requirements served table
description: The slice carries an empty reqs list and the legacy story master carries no requirement id. TSD S5 T8 maps REQ-S5-001 to REQ-S5-005 to FEAT-AST-01 and REQ-S5-006 to REQ-S5-010 to FEAT-AST-08, so no requirement row names FEAT-AST-22 Transfer a pool to RAMC or the joint venture. The story therefore traces to the feature, to FSD S5 A2.22 and to the legacy key, and the requirement table of section 18 carries the placeholder rather than an invented id.
evidence: split_plan.json slice RWB-S5-E4031-APP with reqs as an empty list; legacy_index.json RWB-E4-031 with reqs as an empty list; TSD S5 v2 T8 rows REQ-S5-001 to REQ-S5-010 mapped to FEAT-AST-01 and FEAT-AST-08 only; FSD S5 v3 A1.2 feature overview row FEAT-AST-22 with kind User and first in E4
proposed: Trace the story to FEAT-AST-22, to FSD S5 A2.22 and to RWB-E4-031, and add a requirement row for the feature when the program requirements are next versioned

title: RWB-S5-E4031-CON: the transfer element, the instruction element and the four consumed rows have no published names or fields
source: TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 T3.1, T3.2, T3.3 and T-A.1; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 19, 43 and 45; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 13 and 27; Ownership Map v1 rows asset_sale, listing, asset, recovery_case, approval, partner_instruction and the api row POST /cases/{caseId}/instructions; split_plan.json slice RWB-S5-E4031-CON
description: (1) The pool reference, the transfer-price template version and the committee-approval reference have no column in TSD S5 T3.1, so their property names, types and required flags are unstated and the contract can only declare them as identifiers with the placeholder. (2) The issueInstruction element and its acceptance and refusal codes are unnamed in every source. (3) The case-move answer, the element names of the approval answer and the operation name of the rwb-source-data read are unnamed, so three of the four consumed rows carry the placeholder. (4) No source publishes a REST approval operation, so the approval can only be declared as the answer of the P7 child workflow. (5) The service owns a topic but the step publishes nothing, so the contract must declare an absence that a reader may otherwise read as an omission.
evidence: TSD S5 v2 T3.1 asset_sale DF-SAL-009 to DF-SAL-019 and listing DF-SAL-001 to DF-SAL-008 with no pool, price-version or approval column; TSD S5 v2 T-A.1 with the two read operations only; Architecture v5 slide 19 OUT with the partner activity, the approval child and the two events; Ownership Map v1 api row POST /cases/{caseId}/instructions owner S9 with no element names; split_plan.json slice RWB-S5-E4031-CON with H, C, I and X empty
proposed: Declare the three references as identifiers with the placeholder, keep the four consumed rows with their placeholders and the partner path on the consumed side, declare no approval operation and no event, and tag the baseline when S9, P3 and P7 confirm the names

title: RWB-S5-E4031-CON: the instruction is both a partner REST path and a Temporal activity, and no source reconciles the two
source: Ownership Map v1 api rows POST /cases/{caseId}/instructions, GET /partner/instructions, POST /partner/instructions/{instructionId}/accept and POST /partner/instructions/{instructionId}/results with owner S9; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 19 IN, OUT and notes; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 13, 14 and 27
description: The Ownership Map publishes a partner REST surface for instructions with owner S9, while Architecture v5 slide 19 OUT names TMP Partner: issueInstruction as a Temporal call of rwb-asset and the Temporal and Drools Design model requires the cross-service call of a stage to be an activity on the owner's queue with its answer recorded in history. Both cannot be the call this step makes, no source says which one it is, and the contract has to declare one call type and state what the other surface is.
evidence: Ownership Map v1 api rows POST /cases/{caseId}/instructions, GET /partner/instructions, POST /partner/instructions/{instructionId}/accept and POST /partner/instructions/{instructionId}/results with owner S9; Architecture v5 slide 19 OUT line TMP Partner: issueInstruction (auction vendor); Architecture v5 slide 19 notes tag TMP = Temporal activity or child workflow on the owner's task queue; Temporal and Drools Design v1 slide 13 note each stage is a child workflow started on the owner's queue and slide 27 activity code calls partners
proposed: Declare the Temporal activity as the call this service makes, record the partner REST path as the partner gateway surface rwb-partner uses, and add a drift test that fails a build which declares the partner path on rwb-asset
